capabilities.compatibility: Keep single and multiple selection modes, existing document-generator values, the attach/setValue/setDisabled contract, and the apex:client-change/open/error events during migration. Sorting, incremental paging, recents, grouping, and highlighting are additive presentation features; client choices still resolve through the case-management client archive.
Preserve option labels and phone metadata.
Keep the existing macOS keychain service/account stable so meeting-room booking and chapter applications share credentials and token refresh behavior.

All active-case candidate menus use ApexCasePicker.attach with popup or inline presentation and single or multiple selection. Keep case IDs, full series-child titles, selection callbacks, optional free-text project names, and existing business actions. Sorting and recent selections are shared across pages; client grouping lists multi-client cases under each client. The case-lookup API keeps items and adds bounded offset pagination (has_more, next_offset) plus folder_bound flags; no folder paths are disclosed. Consumers load every page before sorting and render at most 60 additional rows per expansion. Document generators consume case context from their launch URL rather than offering a separate case menu.
Preserve native input values in YYYY-MM-DD form.

Keep light, dark, and user color theme propagation across iframes. A saved theme value of dark or light takes priority across all pages and browser tabs; when no explicit value is saved, initialize and react to system appearance through prefers-color-scheme. Shared color-theme.css and color-theme.js are loaded by child pages; brand accents use kb-theme or apex-accent tokens while destructive and status colors stay semantic.

The existing single and bulk article DELETE endpoints still accept the same requests and report success, but now move article rows and cascading dependencies into recoverable snapshots. Each snapshot expires 30 days after its own deletion time. The background task and trash-list reads purge expired snapshots. Restoring preserves the original article ID and notes, while stale links to separately removed records may be skipped and reported. Uploaded source files remain untouched.

One transparent PNG or WebP logo is shared across color themes. Dark UI surfaces use a cached one-time recolor that lightens neutral strokes, preserves red strokes, and adds a small static red halo; the original source remains unchanged for light mode and the Dock icon. The current logo remains in localStorage for synchronous launch rendering; uploaded history is in IndexedDB. Legacy color-theme logo keys migrate once to history. The global tab bar brand button replaces the visible main tab and invokes the same switchTab('main') action; mobile retains its separate home button. The native brandIcon handler accepts only local application pages and changes the running Dock icon. The packaged Stella icon is built from the approved brand asset; when that same artwork is selected, including a re-encoded copy, the running Dock reuses the bundled icns. Other uploads are rendered with the same inset rounded canvas and packaged through the same multiresolution iconset pipeline before the running Dock icon changes. Keep the existing bundle identifier so WebKit data and macOS permissions remain available. The native client publishes its active logo into ignored data/mobile-brand.json; authenticated settings changes also publish it. Public GET /api/brand and /brand-logo.png contain only branding, while PUT /api/brand requires existing authentication. Mobile clients retain the last logo locally for offline startup, refresh it on connection and foreground, and render dark variants with the shared adapter. Installation icon responses use a white square canvas without a second rounded mask and revalidate instead of retaining a one-day cache. Manifest id remains /case-manager and start_url is /; existing iOS home icons may require re-adding the shortcut. Shell v232 refreshes branding without deleting case caches or pending operations.

Preserve Finder copy/paste, upload, download, and private-mode restrictions. Local file list and search responses may add Finder tag metadata; the case-files page and AI file picker render the seven macOS tag colors, while the case-files context menu may update the selected file or folder's Finder tag color and recursively apply it to descendants when a folder is selected.

Keep at most 200 local display records; files remain the source of truth. Court reading downloads use durable account-scoped backend jobs, separate from the legacy 200-entry display history. Application-material tests are explicitly labeled and never enter the open-dossier source. Closing a page does not cancel downloads; inactive pages stop polling. Account changes pause running and queued jobs.
Keep record IDs routable from macOS notifications.

New events use the apex:* namespace and include a version when their payload is not trivial. The archive picker inside case-files uses apex:archive-picker-ready, apex:archive-selection, and apex:archive-assign-request with version 1, caseId, and relative file paths; the archive workbench replies with apex:archive-status or apex:archive-clear-selection for the same caseId. Both frames check same origin and the expected source frame. Knowledge center uses apex:knowledge-prefill-ask with version 1 and question; the parent checks same origin and the source knowledge tab iframe before filling AI Ask. apex:open-court-downloads carries version 1 and optional jobId; the main host validates same origin and a court-online or download-center source iframe before opening the progress tab.

The apex:page-visibility message is version 1; inactive pages may pause work but must preserve drafts. Low-risk read-only pages may be hibernated after their state is captured; editors, recordings, uploads, CAPTCHA flows and other unsafe pages remain mounted until they implement an explicit snapshot contract.

The public shell contains no case data. Keep the Service Worker scope and /case-manager entry stable, preserve the legal-kb-case-manager IndexedDB schema and pending case-operation queue, validate shell responses before caching, and never clear user data during shell repair. Verified top-level /case-manager navigation enters /?workspace=cases, reusing the existing main tab host and mobile floating navigation; iframe case navigation is never redirected. The public /app-shell endpoint exposes only source UI markup, and its required static assets are public; business APIs remain authenticated. Shell installation must finish preparing the main host even for a fresh signed-out standalone data store. Manifest start_url is / while its identity remains /case-manager. Standalone legacy case HTML enters /?workspace=cases even before a worker controls the page. A same-origin case iframe with expired authentication navigates its parent app to login. The main shell and its versioned assets are prepared independently of browser cookies, and a home-ready marker is published only after every asset succeeds. Offline root navigation ignores query parameters and uses a verified home cache; online login responses remain authoritative.

articles.domains remains the top-level JSON list. GET /api/domains keeps domain and count fields and adds id and children. Article list and detail responses add subcategories with id, name, parent_id and domain alongside subcategory_ids; main article cards and both reader metadata bars display confirmed child labels, with cached catalog resolution for older offline snapshots. Both readers keep source, author, date and label editing outside the collapsible classification labels, visible in both disclosure states with wrapping on narrow screens. Main cards and both reader metadata bars share a single-line label disclosure, showing an expand/collapse button only for overflow and adapting to container resizing. Rules cover every predefined domain and known historical roots, with AI fallback evaluated per domain; migration 16 backfills historical child-topic evidence without changing article assignments. Rules and configured AI discover child suggestions from new and historical articles; known related phrases are consolidated into reusable topics, and automatic proposals enter the review list and can be approved only when at least two distinct articles support a concise topic. Original single-article proposals remain stored. No suggestion enters the approved taxonomy without confirmation. User-selected and excluded classifications and child order survive automatic re-evaluation; source URLs remain article metadata. Deleting a child taxonomy node removes only its article associations, preserves the articles, and suppresses future automatic proposals with the same name under that parent; explicit manual creation clears the suppression. Root deletion remains a separate flow. The unified directory manager owns professional/custom/author editing, with explicit drag handles, insertion boundaries, edge scrolling and Alt/Option keyboard ordering; root dragging temporarily hides child rows and restores them on drop or cancellation without changing expansion preferences; legacy open functions remain adapters. Child rename preserves IDs, keywords and article associations and suppresses old automatic proposals. Reorder requests validate a complete current visible collection and return 409 atomically on duplicates or stale IDs. Offline article snapshot v3 adds subcategory_ids and classification_status without changing IndexedDB keys; older snapshots remain usable for general browsing, but child/pending filters require v3 and the relevant fields. Saved views accept optional subcategoryId, clear absent or deleted child IDs, and retain the parent domain. Expansion mode and paths use the safely parsed legal_kb_directory_state_v1 preference; hovering a root reveals its next level, while hovering a specific child reveals only its own descendants after pointer intent detection; search expansion is temporary. Reclassification preview adds has_changes and subcategory_add/remove by comparing effective assignments, respecting manual selections and exclusions. Matching an existing child or requesting AI alone is not a change. Batched apply skips unchanged articles and adds scanned alongside processed and next_after_id.

Collect aggregate local metrics only; never retain URLs with queries, request bodies, client names, file paths, or case content. Additive metrics may include current and peak memory, aggregate child-process usage, thread/task counts, hibernated-page counts, and coarse case-manager startup stage/timing; child command-line arguments are never collected.

CC2API is additive. cc2api: model IDs use the official Claude Code headless client for Claude Code-only key groups and normalize JSON results into the existing choices contract. The pinned client lives in ignored data/cc2api-runtime; scripts/install_cc2api_runtime.py installs it. Per-call temporary configuration, bare mode, no built-in or MCP tools, and no session persistence isolate the client. Cancellation and timeout kill the child. Keys remain in private config and child environment only. Existing defaults and fallback behavior remain compatible.
